narrative:
The model estimates a 67% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your professional background.

Your total years of experience across all jobs stands out as the strongest factor pushing the model toward predicting you will leave. With 6-10 years overall, you fall into a group where many employees start exploring new opportunities, unlike the majority of those predicted to stay who have only 1-5 years of total experience.

Next, the model noted that you have not received any other job offers while at your current company. This actually works in your favor and pulls the prediction slightly back toward staying, as most employees who remain tend to also lack external offers.

Finally, the length of time you have spent in your current role (1-5 years) also contributes noticeably toward the prediction that you will leave. This is higher than the tenure of many employees the model expects to stay.

Taken together, your broader career experience and current tenure appear to signal that you may be ready for a change, outweighing the stabilizing effect of not having other offers. The organization should discuss your long-term goals with you and explore whether additional responsibilities or clearer advancement paths could increase your commitment. You might also reflect on what would make staying more fulfilling. (218 words)
